source_semantics.question: In an LCU-style assembly of a Hermitian piece, each selected term contributes a scaled controlled-phase source whose upper block carries the intended operator and whose lower-right filler block is normalizer times a phase e^{i*phi}. A source writes both filler phases as e^{i*pi} = -1 and claims the two filler blocks cancel so the clean block equals the intended Hermitian piece S1. Show by direct computation of the lower-right clean entry that the printed all-(-1)-phase choice does NOT cancel, give the exact value of that entry, prove the clean block therefore differs from S1 when the normalizer is nonzero, and exhibit the corrected phase assignment that does make the fillers cancel while preserving the intended operator blocks.
source_semantics.reference_answer: The assembly adds three scaled sources (each scaled by 1/2): a controlled-phase source for A with filler phase, one for A-dagger with filler phase, and a Pauli-X-tensor-B term that has zero lower-right block. The lower-right filler of a scaled controlled-phase source with normalizer N and phase e^{i*phi} is (1/2)*N*e^{i*phi} on the diagonal. With BOTH A and A-dagger terms using phase e^{i*pi} = -1, the lower-right diagonal clean entry is (1/2)*N*(-1) + (1/2)*N*(-1) + 0 = -N. So the printed clean lower-right block equals -N (the identity-filler blocks ADD rather than cancel). But the intended Hermitian piece S1 has lower-right block equal to 0 (S1 is the Hermitian part of the homogenized matrix [[A,B],[0,0]], whose lower-right block is 0). Therefore, if N != 0, the printed clean block has lower-right entry -N != 0 = S1's lower-right entry, so the printed-phase clean block is NOT equal to S1 - a genuine counterexample to the all-(-1) cancellation claim. Corrected assignment: give the two filler phases OPPOSITE signs, e.g. keep the A-dagger term at phase -1 but set the A term's filler phase to 0 (i.e. e^{i*0}=+1) while leaving its upper operator block intact. Then the lower-right clean entry becomes (1/2)*N*(+1) + (1/2)*N*(-1) + 0 = 0, matching S1's zero lower-right block, and the upper A, A-dagger and off-diagonal B blocks are unchanged, so the phase-balanced clean block equals S1 exactly (under the paper's Hermitian B). The lesson: filler phases are a real proof obligation - identical phases add, opposite phases cancel; only a phase-balanced choice recovers the intended block.

source_semantics.question: Let S and T be Hermitian matrices on one finite system and X a Hermitian matrix on a second system. Prove that H=S tensor X+T tensor I is Hermitian without assuming that S and T commute. Give a counterexample showing that the same conclusion can fail if X is not Hermitian.
source_semantics.reference_answer: The adjoint of a tensor product is the tensor product of the adjoints: entrywise, conjugating S(j,i)X(v,u) gives S(i,j)X(u,v) under Hermiticity of both factors. Hence (S tensor X) dagger=S tensor X. Similarly T tensor I is Hermitian because I dagger=I. Adjoint is additive, so H dagger=H. No product S T occurs anywhere in this argument, so S and T need not commute. The premise on X matters: take the first system one-dimensional with S=[1], T=[0], and X=[[0,1],[0,0]]. Then H=X, whereas X dagger=[[0,0],[1,0]] is different. This is an operator-algebra closure result, not a claim that implementing the factors or reading out a simulated evolution is free.
